title: R1-s entity safety (3): three info_player_coop beside the start of every Quake 2 single-player map
cause: With coop set, every co-op player is put at a spawn spot and the spot is telefragged clear: Quake 1 SelectSpawnPoint cycles through the info_player_coop entities and then the info_player_start (progs1996 SelectSpawnPoint 6014-6030; quakec/client.qc:562-572; quakec_ctf/client.qc:526-530) and PutClientInServer calls spawn_tdeath on it (progs1996 6166-6169, spawn_tdeath 10219-10250; quakec/client.qc:807); Quake 2 SelectCoopSpawnPoint gives client N >= 1 the Nth info_player_coop whose targetname matches the (empty) spawnpoint and falls back to the info_player_start (game/p_client.c:831-866, 875-908), and PutClientInServer KillBox-es the spot (game/p_client.c:1247). Generated single-player maps had no info_player_coop, so co-op players 2 and up land on the one start and telefrag. One cause: append three info_player_coop beside the start of every Q1/Q2 single-player map at supported, clear, lit stations facing the start's way.
hypothesis: A Quake 2 single-player map played in co-op puts every co-op player on the one info_player_start, where each spawn telefrags the player before (cited in the cause). Three info_player_coop at supported, clear, lit stations beside the start give players 2 to 4 a spot each; single-player play never reads them, so nothing else in the map or its single-player analyses changes.
expected_mechanism: src/entities.cpp add_single_player_coop_starts (public; include/qmg/entities.hpp) appends kSinglePlayerCoopStarts = 3 PlacementRole::coop_start (new D8 role, appended to the enum) when the switch is on, the game is Quake 1 or Quake 2 and the mode is single-player. EntityAllocator::populate calls it last, after the lights, the Quake 1 camera and the (multiplayer-only) map start, so no earlier placement moves or is renumbered; repair re-runs populate, so the starts survive repair; with the switch off the call returns before any work. Station: start_stations() of change r1s-mp-player-start (feet on the room floor, origin 24 units above it, 32-unit lattice 32 units in from the walls, the 32 x 32 x 56 player box inside the room and overlapping no layout solid or placement volume, >= 64 units on x or y from every other point placement, recomputed after each start so the three keep clear of each other); the start room first, a lit station (a light of the room in clear view) before an unlit one, the station nearest the info_player_start; the rooms joined to the start room only when it has no clear station left; fewer than three stations is a std::runtime_error. Yaw = the start's yaw. Classname from the profiles (classnames.coop_start: info_player_coop in Q1 and Q2; Q3 mapping only, refused by the map builder, validator and visibility analysis). No targetname (direct loads). Analyses: lighting samples them as critical (like the start); navigation treats them as spawns (bound and reachable from the start); visibility samples them at the standing eye but leaves them out of single-player room exposure and spawn safety; quality timing still runs from the start only; the ranker does not count them.

BENCH-v1 cases whose path is a multiplayer path but whose prompt resolves to single_player are therefore in scope; they are listed in mp_path_cases_in_scope. SP-path cases that resolve to a multiplayer mode are out of scope (sp_path_cases_out_of_scope). No MP-sub-lane output change is in flight: r1s-mp-player-start is flipped and recorded as baseline-2.

failures_and_counterexamples_kept: G7 still fails on the 4 multiplayer-path cases that resolve to single player (q1-dm-v3, q1-duel-v3, q2-ctf-v3, q2-duel-v3): they now carry coop starts, but their G7 contract is the multiplayer one; mode resolution is R1-a..R1-d, not this cause
